extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent owners, and patent practitioners (attorneys/agents)
extracted.subtask_description: Quick-reference guidance on the Continuing Application Fee (CAF) under 37 CFR 1.17(w): when it applies, when it is due, how to calculate which tier applies, consequences of non-payment, and special situations (reissue, national stage, certificates of correction).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of the Continuing Application Fee (CAF)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Continuing Application Fee (CAF) is a new fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(w). The CAF is part of the requirements for presenting a benefit claim under § 1.78(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See the FY 2025 Patents Fee Setting Rule preamble and responses to comments for more information (Fee Rule pages cited). The CAF applies to continuing applications (continuation, divisional, continuation-in-part) meeting the timing criteria described below.

rubrics_metrics.name: CAF effective date
rubrics_metrics.description: The CAF set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(w) and the amendments to § 1.78(d) and (e) are effective on January 19, 2025.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules, fee amounts cited at times in the examples reflect rates in effect on Jan 19, 2025; applicants should consult current Fee Schedule for updated amounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: When a CAF is due (general rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Payment of the 37 CFR 1.17(w) fees is required at the time a prompting benefit claim (i.e., a benefit claim that causes the Earliest Benefit Date (EBD) of the later-filed application to be more than six or nine years earlier than its actual filing date) is presented in the later-filed application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the prompting benefit claim is presented at the time of filing, the applicable § 1.17(w) fee is due at filing. If presented later, the fee is due concurrently with presentation of that benefit claim. If the later presentation is by petition for acceptance of an unintentionally delayed benefit claim under § 1.78(e), the § 1.17(w) fee is due in addition to the petition fee under § 1.17(m). See Fee Rule at 91911 and the examples for illustrations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Earliest Benefit Date (EBD)
rubrics_metrics.description: The EBD is the earliest filing date for which benefit is claimed under 35 U.S.C. 120, 121, 365(c), or 386(c), and 37 CFR 1.78(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EBD is determined application-by-application. The EBD cannot be the filing date of a foreign application or the filing date of a provisional application to which benefit is claimed under 35 U.S.C. 119(e). For utility and plant applications, the EBD is also the 'patent term filing date' (the date from which the 20-year patent term is calculated under 35 U.S.C. 154(a)(2)). See Fee Rule citations for further discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: EBD for reissue applications
rubrics_metrics.description: In accordance with 35 U.S.C. 100(i), the EBD of the reissue application is the earliest filing date for which benefit is claimed under 35 U.S.C. 120, 121, 365(c), or 386(c), and 37 CFR 1.78(d) in the original patent for which reissue is sought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples in the guide (Examples 19–21) illustrate how reissue and continuing reissue situations affect CAF applicability and waivers.

rubrics_metrics.name: CAF applicability to application types (continuing, national stage, reissue)
rubrics_metrics.description: The CAF applies to all utility, plant, and design continuing applications (continuation, divisional, continuation-in-part) that have an actual filing date more than six years after their EBD. National stage applications filed under 35 U.S.C. 371 are subject to CAF. Reissue applications are subject to CAF as described below.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Fee Rule at cited pages and examples (Examples 5–8, 19–21) for national stage and reissue illustrations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect on applications filed before the effective date
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications filed before January 19, 2025, can be subject to CAF only if a benefit claim is presented on or after the effective date and the application meets the timing parameters in 37 CFR 1.17(w) as a result of that or any other benefit claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An application pending prior to the effective date will not incur a fee based on any benefit claims properly presented prior to the effective date. However, if a benefit claim is presented on or after the effective date, the CAF may be due even if that presentation does not change the EBD (see Fee Rule at 91912 and Examples 12–14).

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver for non-continuing reissue applications (previously entered benefit claims)
rubrics_metrics.description: For non-continuing reissue applications, 37 CFR 1.17(w) is waived to the following extent: If a benefit claim was properly presented and entered in the original patent, it will not be considered to be presented for purposes of the CAF when it is included in an ADS upon filing of an application for reissue of the original patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This waiver means a non-continuing reissue that only repeats a previously-entered benefit claim does not trigger CAF (see Example 19). The waiver does not apply if other benefit claims are presented on or after the effective date (Examples 20–21).

rubrics_metrics.name: Adding a benefit claim via certificate of correction
rubrics_metrics.description: If the application that issued as the patent had an actual filing date that is more than six years after its EBD, adding a benefit claim in a patent via a certificate of correction can trigger the CAF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Correction of a patent with respect to a benefit claim requires conditions under MPEP 1481.03 and a petition under 37 CFR 1.78(e). As amended, such petitions require both the petition fee under § 1.17(m) and any applicable CAF. See Fee Rule at 91986–87 and Example 15.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequence of not paying the CAF when due
rubrics_metrics.description: If a CAF is not paid when it is due, the consequence is non-entry of the entire benefit claim (same as other deficiencies under § 1.78(d)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the benefit claim is not entered due to non-payment, applicant must present the benefit claim again with the applicable CAF if they still desire the benefit claim (see Examples 14, 16, 17, and 18). See MPEP 211.02(a) for correcting/adding a benefit claim after filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to verify whether a benefit claim was entered
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant can verify whether a particular benefit claim was entered by checking the application’s Filing Receipt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If entered, the benefit claim will appear in the 'Domestic Priority data as claimed by applicant' section of the Filing Receipt. Applicants should carefully and promptly review filing receipts to avoid the need for a petition under 37 CFR 1.78 and the petition fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple benefit claims and how fees are computed
rubrics_metrics.description: The fees in 37 CFR 1.17(w) are based on the application’s EBD, not the number of benefit claims made. Presenting multiple benefit claims at the same time will not incur multiple fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If benefit claims are presented at multiple times during pendency, a second fee may be due if a later-presented benefit claim changes the EBD to be more than nine years earlier than the actual filing date. In that situation, the amount due under § 1.17(w)(2) for the later presentation will reflect any prior payment under § 1.17(w)(1) (i.e., prior amounts are subtracted). Examples 9–11 and 16–18 illustrate timing and arithmetic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Which CAF tier is owed and interaction with prior payments
rubrics_metrics.description: The maximum amount due in a single application or patent is the § 1.17(w)(2) fee. If a previously-paid § 1.17(w)(1) fee was paid and a later change prompts § 1.17(w)(2), the amount owed is the difference between § 1.17(w)(2) and the amount previously paid under § 1.17(w)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a newly-presented benefit claim does not change the EBD to more than nine years earlier than filing, no additional CAF is due because the § 1.17(w)(1) was already paid. See Examples 10, 13, 17, and 18 for illustrations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing on weekend or Federal holiday that falls on CAF anniversary
rubrics_metrics.description: If the 6-year or 9-year anniversary of an application’s EBD falls on a weekend or a Federal holiday within the District of Columbia, 35 U.S.C. 21(b) and 37 CFR 1.7 permit filing on the next business day without incurring the applicable CAF tier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically: if the 6-year anniversary falls on a weekend/holiday, filing on the next business day avoids incurring a CAF under § 1.17(w). If the 9-year anniversary falls on a weekend/holiday, filing on the next business day avoids the § 1.17(w)(2) second-tier and instead the § 1.17(w)(1) first-tier would be due.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee amounts, discounts, and checking current Fee Schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: Fee amounts shown in the guide are those in effect on January 19, 2025: § 1.17(w)(1) = $2,700 and § 1.17(w)(2) = $4,000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discounts are available for most patent fees as shown in the Fee Rule and on the USPTO Fee Schedule. Fee amounts may change over time; applicants and patent owners should check the current Fee Schedule on the USPTO website when determining appropriate amounts to pay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing when insufficient or incorrect CAF payment
rubrics_metrics.description: When the appropriate § 1.17(w) fee is not paid or authorized for charge to a deposit account, the USPTO will not enter benefit claims that require that fee; benefit claims not requiring the fee may still be entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Filing Receipt will reflect only the benefit claims that were entered. Non-entry of specific benefit claims can change the application’s EBD (see Examples 16 and 17). Applicants should monitor Filing Receipts and correct by presenting the claim with the applicable fee if needed.
